title: 10th Day with Options Trading Bot
author: VegetableReception34
selftext:
I've been building a SPY options trading bot that actually takes control of my screen, reads live TradingView charts, and makes trading decisions based on what it sees.

For entries, it uses the 9/21 EMA, VWAP, and GEX levels to identify setups.

Risk management is pretty straightforward. I have a 30% stop loss, and profits are taken in stages at 25%, 50%, and 100%. The 50% target has a 5% trailing stop, while the 100% target has a 25% trailing stop.

Things were going well until Friday, when some of my chart indicators failed to load. Instead of recognizing that the data was missing and skipping the trade, the bot made up an entry signal and took a bad setup.

That mistake cost me 30% on the day.

It's one thing to build a bot that can trade. It's another to make sure it knows when **not to trade**, especially when the information it relies on isn't there.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
the bot making up an entry when the indicators didn't load is the scary line here. a missing input should be a hard no trade, never a blank the model guesses at.

I built Quantradin on the same principle: a rule whose input isn't there doesn't fire, and options pay the quoted spread. free, no real money. quantradin.com

when the chart failed, did the bot see an empty GEX level or a stale one?

comments.author: Alphanet_dogwalker
comments.body: I wouldn't leave the missing-indicator check to the same model that invented the signal. The order code should refuse new entries unless the required inputs are present and current. Test it with a deliberately broken chart too. A better prompt might help, but it shouldn't be the only thing between a blank indicator and a live order.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Good lesson to share. I'd make the bot fail closed: if any indicator is missing, stale or can't be read, the code should block the trade, with no way for the model to fill in the gap. Reading charts from the screen is fragile, so a data feed is safer, and a few weeks in paper mode would show how often things don't load. Cymetica lets you connect your own AI agent and starts it in paper mode first, which suits this kind of testing.
